statement: "Lucky Day" is the fourth episode of the fifteenth series of the British science-fiction television series Doctor Who.
It was written by Pete McTighe.
It was directed by Peter Hoar.
The episode was released on BBC iPlayer, BBC One and Disney+ on 3 May 2025.
It features the return of companion Ruby Sunday (Millie Gibson).
Ruby Sunday (Millie Gibson) plays a leading role in the episode opposite Conrad Clark (Jonah Hauer-King).
The Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) and Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu) are the series' main leads.
The Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) and Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu) only appear briefly in the episode.
The episode focuses on Ruby.
Ruby begins a relationship with podcaster Conrad Clark.
Ruby attempts to find her place in the world after leaving the Doctor.
Conrad's true aim is to turn the public against military organisation UNIT.
Ruby and Kate Lethbridge-Stewart have to deal with the repercussions of Conrad's actions when his true aim is revealed.
"Lucky Day" was devised by showrunner Russell T Davies.
Davies enlisted McTighe to write it.
McTighe used the episode to develop Ruby and Kate's characters.
McTighe used the episode to explore the spread and effects of online hatred.
The episode's monster, the Shreek, was based on McTighe's childhood fears of dog-like creatures in the dark.
The Shreek was portrayed via costume and an animatronic head.
Filming took place in November 2023 in Newton, Porthcawl and at Wolf Studios Wales.
It was filmed back-to-back with the series premiere.
"Lucky Day" received positive reviews from critics.
Critics highlighted Gibson's performance.
Critics highlighted the twist regarding Conrad's true motives.
Critics highlighted the episode's social commentary.
Critics were more critical of underdeveloped plotlines.
Critics were more critical of the execution of Conrad as an antagonist.
The Doctor and his companion Belinda Chandra arrive on New Year's Day 2007.
The Doctor and his companion Belinda Chandra meet 8-year-old Conrad Clark.
Over the next several years, Conrad investigates sightings of the Doctor and his ship the TARDIS.
An adult Conrad eventually sees the Doctor with his then-companion Ruby Sunday in 2024.
Conrad is marked as prey by a creature called the Shreek in 2024.
In 2025, Ruby stopped travelling with the Doctor.
Ruby gives Conrad an interview on his podcast about her encounters with extraterrestrial life.
Ruby and Conrad start dating.
Ruby gives Conrad an antidote to prevent him from being hunted by the Shreek.
The Shreek has recently been captured by military organisation UNIT.
During a weekend at Conrad's home village, Ruby tells Conrad she is suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder following her experiences with the Doctor.
Two Shreek appear in pursuit of Conrad.
Conrad admits he did not take the antidote.
Ruby calls UNIT and their leader Kate Lethbridge-Stewart to the village.
The Shreek are revealed to be actors in costumes.
The Shreek are part of a group led by Conrad that seeks to discredit UNIT.
Conrad's relationship with Ruby was a ploy to further his plans.
Conrad and his team frame the scene negatively towards UNIT.
Media and social media coverage turn against UNIT.
Conrad and his followers continue to perpetuate disinformation.
The disinformation claims that UNIT is committing fraud.
The disinformation claims that aliens do not exist.
Kate realises Conrad has an insider in UNIT.
The insider sneaks Conrad into the UNIT headquarters.
Kate allows Conrad to reach the command floor.
Conrad livestreams his intrusion.
Kate releases the Shreek in order to expose Conrad's lies.
The Shreek hunts Conrad.
With the Shreek attacking him, Conrad admits on his livestream he has been lying about UNIT.
Ruby stuns the Shreek.
Conrad backtracks on that admission.
The Shreek bites Conrad's arm.
Public sentiment turns in UNIT's favour.
Kate's higher ups believe she went too far in releasing the Shreek.
Ruby decides to get away from UNIT to overcome her trauma.
Kate offers Ruby her support.
Conrad is imprisoned.
Conrad is visited by the Doctor.
The Doctor hails from a point in time before he met Belinda.
The Doctor berates Conrad for spreading lies.
The Doctor berates Conrad for harming Ruby and his friends.
The Doctor tells Conrad that he will die in prison.
The Doctor tells Conrad that he will be forgotten by history.
After the Doctor leaves, a woman named Mrs Flood releases Conrad from jail.
Doctor Who showrunner Russell T Davies wished to include an episode discussing the spread of toxicity and hatred on the internet.
Russell T Davies contacted writer Pete McTighe to write the script.
The two first talked over FaceTime.
They later talked on Zoom as McTighe was abroad in Australia.
Davies sent McTighe viewing copies of the three 60th anniversary specials before any of those episodes had been publicly released.
Davies sent McTighe viewing copies of the 2023 Christmas special before any of those episodes had been publicly released.
Davies sent McTighe viewing copies of the entirety of the fourteenth series before any of those episodes had been publicly released.
Davies sent these copies so that McTighe could better understand Ruby's character development.
Prior to penning "Lucky Day", McTighe had written the eleventh and twelfth series episodes "Kerblam!" and "Praxeus" under previous Doctor Who showrunner Chris Chibnall.
McTighe and fellow fifteenth series writer Inua Ellams were additionally involved in earlier development of the thirteenth run of episodes with Chibnall.
The thirteenth run of episodes was forcibly shortened by the COVID-19 pandemic.
The shortened thirteenth run of episodes became the six-part Flux serial.
When writing the episode, McTighe said that he wanted to take the opportunity to explore what happens to a companion after they leave the Doctor.
McTighe felt that exploring what happens to a companion after they leave the Doctor had infrequently been done in the show's past.
McTighe described the episode as a mix between action, romantic comedy, and gothic horror.
He compared one of the main settings to the village Devil's End from the 1971 Third Doctor serial, The Dæmons.
McTighe believed that, with the story being Ruby-centric, it made it similar to the 2024 episode "73 Yards".
Conrad and his followers refer to themselves as "Think Tank".
McTighe revealed "Think Tank" to be a reference to a group with the same name in the 1974–1975 Fourth Doctor serial, Robot.
Ruby was referred to as having post-traumatic stress disorder following her time with the Doctor.
Davies wanted to portray Ruby's post-traumatic stress disorder in the episode.
"Lucky Day" allowed McTighe to explore Kate's character further.
McTighe stated Kate's willingness to go too far would have further repercussions "beyond this episode, beyond this season, even beyond this show."
McTighe developed the Shreek from his childhood fears of dog-like creatures in darkness.
The conceptual idea for the Shreek was based on a terrifying "four-legged, creeping animal" that had a desire to hunt and could not be reasoned with.
Prior to "Lucky Day", the Shreek were first mentioned in Caged, a 2024 Doctor Who novel by Una McCormack.
A number of Easter egg references to past episodes and popular culture were included in Lucky Day.
It is a "Doctor-light" episode.
"Doctor-light" is a term within the programme to describe instalments which feature the Doctor minimally.
Davies stated this required them to find "inventive ways" to include the Doctor.
One inventive way to include the Doctor is a flashback to an unseen story set during the previous series.
The Doctor's scene with Conrad at the end of the episode takes place before the Doctor meets Belinda Chandra.
This reveals how the Doctor had prior knowledge of Belinda Chandra in "The Robot Revolution".
The read-through for "Lucky Day" took place at Wolf Studios Wales on 7 November 2023.
Attendees noted a unique atmosphere due to unaware cast members' response to Conrad's reveal as a villain.
Millie Gibson returns as outgoing series regular and former companion Ruby Sunday.
It was the first of three appearances that Gibson makes during the fifteenth series.
It was Gibson's first appearance since the 2024 Christmas special, "Joy to the World".
In July 2024, at the Doctor Who San Diego Comic-Con panel, it was officially announced that Jonah Hauer-King had been cast in a role that would be involved in Ruby's character arc.
Further details later revealed that Hauer-King would portray Conrad, a podcaster and Ruby's boyfriend.
Following the episode's broadcast, Gibson revealed in an interview that Hauer-King's character would also appear later on in the series.
Ncuti Gatwa and Varada Sethu also make brief appearances as the fifteenth incarnation of the Doctor and his companion, Belinda Chandra, respectively.
Paul Jerricho, who plays Alfie in the story, previously held the role of the Castellan in "The Five Doctors" (1983).
Lachele Carl reprised her role as newsreader Trinity Wells.
Alex Jones appears as herself.
Alex Jones is a Welsh presenter on The One Show.
Alex Jones interviews Conrad.
The remainder of the guest cast includes Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge-Stewart.
The remainder of the guest cast includes Ruth Madeley as Shirley Bingham.
The remainder of the guest cast includes Michelle Greenidge as Carla.
The remainder of the guest cast includes Angela Wynter as Cherry Sunday.
The remainder of the guest cast includes Alexander Devrient as Colonel Christofer Ibrahim.
The remainder of the guest cast includes Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood.
Nicholas Briggs is also featured in a voice role as the Vlinx.
The primary Shreek costume was constructed using fibreglass molds and clay.
The final molds were eventually injected with silicon and painted.
The Shreek uses an animatronic head.
The Shreek costumes used by Conrad's friends were designed as imitative versions of the original.
The imitative Shreek costumes looked similar to an extent.
The imitative Shreek costumes were intentionally fake.
The design team at Millennium FX had a designer look at the primary Shreek costume once.
The designer then constructed this derivative version from memory to reflect the costumes' in-universe construction.
The team had to make the costumes look convincing while also looking like "rubber costumes".
Making the costumes look convincing while also looking like "rubber costumes" proved a challenge.
The Shreek performers were unable to see inside the mask of the Shreek costume.
Outside direction was required for the actors to know where they needed to go.

The inclusion of mannequins in the scene where Conrad explores the abandoned department store featuring the Shreek was a result of McTighe wanting to include a callback to the first episode of Doctor Who's revival, "Rose" (2005).
"Rose" (2005) featured living mannequins called Autons.
Costume designer Pam Downe designed Ruby's outfits with dark blue and green colours.
Gibson felt the dark blue and green colours were "more mature colours".
One of Ruby's outfits included a pinstripe suit and pants.
Gibson said the pinstripe suit and pants were reminiscent of one of David Tennant's previous outfits in the series.
"Lucky Day" was directed by Peter Hoar.
The episode was placed in the second production block of the fifteenth series with the first episode, "The Robot Revolution".
The episode followed recording of "Joy to the World" in the block immediately preceding.
The two episodes in this block were filmed concurrently.
They were filmed concurrently by utilising a back-to-back filming technique.
Principal photography for the episode began on 14 November 2023.
Gibson and Hauer-King were spotted filming scenes together a day later.
Location filming was done in Cardiff City Centre on 24 November.
The production team made use of Howells department store for the abandoned department store scene.
Howells department store was similarly used as a filming location in "Rose".
For the scenes set in the village, the town of Newton, Porthcawl, was used.
Recording took place from 27–29 November in Newton, Porthcawl.
Two-thirds of the budget allocated to the six-week filming block was used during those three days.
Three hours of those three days were spent shooting three takes with a helicopter.
Soundstage recording was done at Wolf Studios Wales.
A former authorised firearms officer was present on set as a weapons master.
Real firearms with blank cartridges were utilised during filming.
Hoar originally hoped to re-use the helipad set that was constructed for "The Giggle" (2023) for the scene where Conrad breaks into the UNIT Tower.
The helipad set had been torn down after production concluded on "The Giggle" (2023).
There were not enough funds to rebuild the helipad set.
A Steadicam was ultimately used to film to make following Conrad easier.
McTighe's initial script included extras of Conrad's followers entering the tower with him.
The number of people for the scene had to be reduced for feasibility.
Two Shreek performers were kept on set.
One Shreek performer specialized in movement.
The other Shreek performer specialized in action.
The crew struggled with getting the Shreek's mouth to open wide enough to bite Conrad.
A pre-broken window also had to be fabricated.
Stunt glass is not fabricated in sizes large enough for the window frame.
"Lucky Day" was simultaneously released on BBC iPlayer at 8 a.m. British Summer Time (BST) in the United Kingdom.
"Lucky Day" was simultaneously released on Disney+ in the United States at 12 a.m. Pacific Daylight Time on 3 May 2025.
A BBC One broadcast of the episode followed at 7:10 p.m. BST.
Disney also handled international distribution of the episode.
In the United Kingdom, the episode recorded overnight broadcast ratings of 1.5 million.
The ratings were a decline on the previous episodes.
The ratings set a new record low after "Lux"'s 1.58 million.
"Lucky Day" had been seen by a total of 2.80 million after seven days.
The 2.80 million total includes catch-up viewing on iPlayer.
On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 70% of 10 critics' reviews are positive.
Robert Anderson, writing for IGN, praised the episode's writing.
Robert Anderson praised the performance of Gibson.
Robert Anderson praised the usage of Conrad as an antagonist.
Robert Anderson stated that the episode at times could feel "hollow".
Robert Anderson stated that Ruby's character arc was not as well executed as it could have been.
Daniel Cooper, writing for Engadget, highlighted the twist about Conrad's identity.
Daniel Cooper highlighted McTighe's writing.
Daniel Cooper highlighted the episode's social commentary.
Daniel Cooper felt Conrad's backstory utilising "the trope that survivors of abuse perpetuate that cycle of abuse" was overused.
Adi Tantimedh, writing for Bleeding Cool, praised the episode.
Adi Tantimedh highlighted the twist involving Conrad.
Adi Tantimedh highlighted the episode's social commentary.
Stefan Mohammed, writing for Den of Geek, found several of the episode's plot points underdeveloped.
Stefan Mohammed believed that Ruby's decision to leave UNIT was not justified by her relationship with family and Kate.
Stefan Mohammed believed that Conrad embodying all aspects of the social issues being discussed made him feel overcomplicated with unclear motivations.
Despite this, Stefan Mohammed found Gibson's performance compelling.
Stefan Mohammed highlighted the episode's usage of Kate.
Vicky Jessop, writing for the London Standard, penned a positive review for the episode.
Vicky Jessop felt Conrad's execution as an antagonist was weak.
Vicky Jessop felt the consequences of his actions were not explored well enough.
Isobel Lewis from The A.V. Club opined that the episode had consistency issues not present in the rest of the series.
Isobel Lewis also found the plot as being too similar to "73 Yards".
Isobel Lewis negatively compared "Lucky Day" to "73 Yards".
